thread:
incident_bot: Pager alert — elevated 5xx + latency observed in AWS eu-central-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. 5xx rate: 12% (10m), p95 latency: 1.9s. Paging: @ryan_oncall @anna_sre. Links: https://observability.redwood.internal/alerts/6939991234, logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q=eu-central-1+5xx
ryan_oncall: Ack, I'm on it. Pulling dashboard and recent deploys now.
anna_sre: I'm seeing STS/auth upstream 502/503 spikes from eu-central1 in traces. A lot of control-plane retries and token-exchange timeouts.
dmitri_infra: Terraform/infra metrics show NAT gateway error spikes and increased ELB 502s in eu-central1 since ~6939987600. Possible provider-side degradation.
ryan_oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) Fail-route Hosted API traffic from eu-central-1 -> eu-west-1 (emergency routing). 2) Drain Dedicated pools in eu-central-1 and shift capacity to eu-west-1. 3) Post incident on status page and notify impacted customers. Executing step 1 now.
ryan_oncall: Runbook ops commands I'm applying:
```
# emergency routing switch
/ops/routing shift --from-region eu-central-1 --to-region eu-west-1 --mode emergency
# pause new host allocations in eu-central-1
kubectl -n redwood scale deployment model-serving --replicas=0 -l region=eu-central-1
# increase burst pool in eu-west-1
/infra/dedicated scale --region eu-west-1 --add-nodes 2 --reason "eu-central1 egress failures"
```
anna_sre: Starting prefix cache warmup and KV cache priming in eu-west-1. Expect ~60-90s before steady state.
julia_support: Drafting customer comms for affected orgs: "We're seeing elevated errors and latency for EU-hosted endpoints; traffic is being routed to eu-west-1 as a temporary mitigation. No data loss expected. We will update in ~15m." Should I send now?
ryan_oncall: Yes, go ahead and send. Use severity level: "Degraded — third-party dependency (AWS)". Add link to status page once posted.
status_bot: Incident created on status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-6939991234-eu-central1-auth-egress
julia_support: Message posted to affected customers and ticketing triage started. :thumbsup:
anna_sre: Snippet from traces showing STS upstream failures:
```
trace_id=abc12345 status=502 upstream=sts.amazonaws.com latency=1243ms
trace_id=abc12346 status=503 upstream=sts.amazonaws.com latency=987ms
```
dmitri_infra: Observing dedicated pool allocations failing to attach in eu-central-1 with control-plane 5xx. That's why we need to shift nodes out. Kicking off reallocation now.
ryan_oncall: p95 down from 1.9s -> 720ms within 4m after routing change, 5xx down from 12% -> 3.4%. Continuing to monitor for flapping.
anna_sre: Keep routing in place for 30m post-stabilization. If metrics remain stable, we'll slowly revert to original routing with canary percentages.
dmitri_infra: Dedicated pool actions: +2 nodes in eu-west-1 added, draining eu-central-1 pool. ETA for full capacity shift ~12m.
anna_sre: Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m, handing over to @oncall_jeff for overnight monitoring. Summary: root cause appears to be AWS regional auth/egress failures causing control-plane and NAT errors; we've rerouted traffic, warmed caches, scaled alternative region.
oncall_jeff: Taking over. Ack — I'll watch the alerting channels. If 5xx rises above 5% or p95 >1s, I'll escalate to infra. Contact list pinned.
julia_support: I'll keep customers updated every 30 minutes until normal.
ryan_oncall: Thanks team. Logging runbook and postmortem stub: https://playbooks.redwood.internal/runbooks/aws-region-egress.
status_bot: Incident severity set to "High - third-party outage". Next update in 15m.
anna_sre: Final note before handoff: no evidence of data compromise, impact limited to request failures and latency for EU region. We'll capture traces for postmortem.
oncall_jeff: :ok_hand: continuing monitoring, will ping if anything regresses."
